newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG's Highlands Pacific details float plans.
newsitem.headline: PNG's Highlands Pacific details float plans.

text.p: Papua New Guinea (PNG) resources group Highlands Pacific Ltd said on Monday it would offer about 76.5 million shares to investors and institutions as part of its plan to raise A$190 million in a share market float.

The company said five PNG institutions had committed to subscribing for 72.7 million shares. Of the remaining 3.8 million shares, preference would be given to Highland Pacific employees in relation to 500,000 and then to PNG residents.
Highlands Pacific was born from a restructure proposal put forward by Highlands Gold Ltd after a takeover offer by Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc late last year.
Highlands Gold has previously stated the Highlands Pacific float would raise A$190 million through the issue of 190 million shares at A$1 each.

The company said 113.5 million shares were to be offered to shareholders of Highlands Gold, whose shares were acquired by Placer Dome. Highlands Pacific said it would consider issuing up to another 20 million if the offer was oversubscribed.
The offer is due to open on April 24, to close on May 22, with an expected listing date of June 13.

Under the Highlands Gold plan, Placer Dome would control Highlands Gold's 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in PNG, while Highlands Pacific would buy the group's remaining assets in PNG and Indonesia.
Placer won control of Highlands Gold with a 75 cent a share offer and Highlands Gold shareholders would recieve a three-for-10 entitlement in the new company.
